# week 8

- quiz: 100% of the data is not tested on 10 fold cross validation. 10 fold cross validation is preferred over 80/20 because all of the observations are seen, so there are no unlucky splits.
- beta coefficient: a 1% increase goes with the coefficient more in y
- error: broken fold
    - small fold had all of its data in one, so it couldn’t be predicted since that data wasn’t seen.
    - solution: merge small groups before cross-validation
    - usually happens in neighborhoods
- points for prediction
    - average distance to the nearest occurrence
    - avg distance to the _ nearest occurrences
    - KNN: K nearest neighbors
    - buffer around each house and the number of occurrences within that buffer
- clean the data, the smaller, the better fit
    - ex. $1 homes, really expensive ones → may lead to overfitting
    - fresh data with outliers won’t work on this model
    - can make indicator variables (houses with more than 5+ bedrooms = mansion)
- spatial lag: neighbors average
    - every house gets average residual of 5 nearest neighbors
- positive slope on Moran’s I, relationship with each house and the neighbors
    - equation: if i’m above average, will my neighbors above average too?
- spatial autocorrelation
    - -1 more spread out than it is in real life
- [moran.mc](http://moran.mc) shuffles the residuals across houses n times and if the real i beats almost all the shuffle → clustering is not luck.
